newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Ethnic Albanians on trial in tense Serb province.
newsitem.headline: Ethnic Albanians on trial in tense Serb province.

text.p: Eighteen ethnic Albanians, accused of hostile activity and planning terrorist acts, went on trial on Monday in Pristina, the capital of Serbia's troubled province of Kosovo.
The Democratic League of Kosovo (LDK), the biggest ethnic Albanian party in Kosovo, said all but two of the defendants had been in custody since January.
They have been indicted for alleged involvement in hostile activities and affiliation with a clandestine organisation, the National Movement for the Liberation of Kosovo.
The indictments allege the defendants wanted to use force to make Kosovo secede from Serbia. The defendants deny the charges, independent Belgrade news agency Beta reported.
Kosovo, where ethnic Albanians outnumber Serbs nine to one, is widely regarded as a powder keg which, if ignited, could damage international peace efforts in the Balkans.
Some 30 people, both Serbs and Albanians, have been killed over the past year in guerrilla violence. Two Serbian policeman were seriously injured in an ambush near Pristina over the weekend.

Serbian police cracked down on the province in January arresting some 70 people in a widely-pubicised sweep following the guerrilla attacks. LDK, which advocates peaceful resistance to Serb rule, says up to 55 people are still in Serb custody and alleges some have been tortured.

In March, Serbian authorities indicted 15 ethnic Albanians on charges of terrorism, killing three policemen and one Serb civilian, and attempting to murder 16 other people. That group has yet to go on trial.

Serbia revoked Kosovo's autonomy in 1989, claiming its Albanian population wanted to secede and join neighbouring Albania. The Albanians, led by Ibrahim Rugova, head of the LDK, have boycotted Serbian institutions since.
Albanian parties deny the existence of terrorist groups and say those arrested are victims of Serb persecution.

But American intelligence officials believe an ethnic Albanian group -- the Kosovo Liberation Army, a shadowy group about which little is known -- has staged at least five armed attacks in the last year and has the potential to disrupt Serb control of Kosovo.

The KLA released a proclamation over the weekend calling "citizens of the Republic of Kosovo to reject the peace-making policy of the Kosovo Albanian leader Ibrahim Rugova... and accept the liberation struggle against the invader".
It threatened severe reprisals against Albanians who cooperated with the Serbs and those financing the LDK, demanding money for its own cause.
